subject: Textiles
examFormat: Three papers, all to be taken; Papers 1 and 2 form a composite paper taken at one sitting. Paper 1: forty multiple-choice objective questions in 50 minutes for 40 marks. Paper 2: six essay-type questions, four to be answered in 2 hours for 60 marks. Paper 3: two practical projects of which one is executed within five days, six hours each day, for 80 marks; questions are sent two weeks earlier for sketches and preparatory notes, which carry 20 marks, making 100 marks in total.
excluded: The item 'Renowned Ghanaian Textile Artists' under Introduction to Textiles (Ghana-specific).

topics.name: Introduction to Textiles
objectives: Explain the meaning/rationale for studying textiles
Describe the developments of textiles and careers
Explain textiles and cultural values
Describe the competencies, attitudes and behaviour of students for employment and customers

topics.name: Textile Fibres and Yarns
objectives: Identify and classify fibres
State the properties and suitability of fibres
Describe fibre processing, e.g. soaking, ginning
Describe yarn preparation, traditional and contemporary
Identify types of yarn
Describe blends and mixtures
Use yarn terminologies

topics.name: Fabric Construction Processes
objectives: Prepare point paper designs: plain, twill, satin/sateen and variations
Describe looms and accessories: types of loom (man power, traditional, broad loom and power looms, e.g. shuttle and shuttleless loom)
Carry out textile calculations: weight/cost of warp, weft and fabric
Describe weaving processes (traditional and broad loom): warping, beaming, heddling, reeding, tying up, bobbin winding etc., and loom motions (primary, secondary and auxiliary)
Describe other fabric construction processes: knitting, crocheting and tapestry
Describe non-woven fabric

topics.name: Fabric Decoration and Finishing Techniques
objectives: Prepare, care for and maintain tools, materials and equipment
Make basic drawings using the elements and principles of design
Develop ideas and preliminary designs, including the use of ICT
Use indigenous colour schemes, ideas, symbols and cultural motifs for designing
Apply decorative techniques: dyeing, printing, appliqué and embroidery processes and equipment
Identify types of finishing techniques: mechanical and chemical
Care for and maintain fabrics

topics.name: Sustainable Development
objectives: Describe challenges and interventions in managing resources, marketing and distribution
Explain cultural values (traditional/contemporary)
Observe healthy studio practices

topics.name: Portfolio and Exhibition
objectives: Identify types of portfolios: hard and soft copy
Collect and build a portfolio
Explain the meaning, types, purpose and processes of mounting exhibitions
Appreciate and patronize indigenous textiles

topics.name: Entrepreneurial Skills in Practice
objectives: Prepare a business plan
Plan an enterprise
State the key points of a business plan
Cost, price and market textile products
